strengths: Novel and important problem setting: The paper introduces two under-explored yet crucial capabilities for mobile GUI agents—proactive task suggestion and personalized task execution—moving the literature beyond passive instruction-following on synthetic tasks.

Realistic, longitudinal dataset: FingerTip 20K contains over 21,000 multi-step interaction episodes across 506 apps collected from 95 real users on their daily physical Android devices over a month, capturing authentic user intents, temporal patterns, and contextual metadata (time, location, user profiles).

Thorough empirical analysis and baselines: The benchmark evaluates a wide suite of generalist models, reasoning models, and specialized GUI agents, complemented by human baselines and systematic ablations (e.g., impact of context elements, initial screenshots, out-of-domain generalization).

Human validation of benchmark components: The paper provides meaningful human validation studies, including a human baseline for intent prediction (30.3% vs. 12.8% for best model) and a user study validating the automated personalization metric (Sim2) against human preference ratings.
weaknesses: Geographic and ecosystem concentration: All 95 crowd-workers and apps are drawn from mainland China and the Chinese Android ecosystem, which may introduce domain-specific interaction patterns and limits immediate empirical transferability to global app ecosystems.

Scale of interactive evaluation: Due to the complexity and manual overhead of running tests on physical devices connected via ADB and inspecting final states, the task execution test set is relatively small (200 episodes).

Automated metrics for open-ended tasks: Measuring proactive intent prediction relies partly on LLM-as-a-judge (DeepSeek-V3), which can introduce judgment variances, and string edit distance (Levenshtein) on action sequences can be sensitive to extraneous UI noise (e.g., accidental clicks, minor scrolling variations) rather than true user style.

strengths: Compelling and timely motivation: While almost all existing mobile GUI benchmarks evaluate reactive instruction-following, this paper introduces two fresh, practically relevant dimensions: proactive task suggestion and personalized task execution.

Substantial and realistic longitudinal dataset: FingerTip 20K collects 21,437 episodes from 95 users over a full month across 506 apps on real Android devices, complete with real-world contextual metadata (timestamps, location/scenario, user profile, and temporal histories).

Comprehensive benchmark experiments: The paper evaluates a wide array of both generalist MLLMs (GPT-4.1, Qwen variants, DeepSeek-VL2) and specialized GUI agents (UI-TARS, CogAgent, Aguvis, AppAgent, AutoDroid), providing a clear snapshot of current state-of-the-art capabilities and revealing large human-agent performance gaps (e.g., 12.8% vs. 30.3% in proactive suggestion).

Thorough supplementary analyses: The appendix provides extensive ablations and validations, including user studies validating the automated personalization metric (Sim2), probability distribution formulation of intents, and out-of-domain generalization across unseen users, apps, and intents.
weaknesses: Reproducibility and dynamism of the physical device environment: The personalized task execution benchmark relies on real Chinese third-party Android apps running on physical phones via ADB. Because live mobile apps constantly update UI elements, network states, and dynamic content, replicating the exact execution evaluation across future models poses notable challenges.

Demographic and geographic specificity: As acknowledged in the limitations, all participants and apps are situated within mainland China's app ecosystem. UI navigation patterns, app ecosystems (super-apps like WeChat/Alipay), and linguistic habits may not immediately generalize to other global mobile environments.

Formulation and evaluation of proactive intent prediction: In the 0-screenshot setting, predicting exact intent descriptions from user profile and recent history is an inherently open-ended and low-probability task (evidenced by low success rates across all models, and only 30.3% for humans). While the probability distribution setting explored in Appendix A.6.5 is much more natural and actionable for real-world assistive agents, it is currently relegated to the appendix rather than explored in the main paper.

strengths: Compelling and timely problem formulation: Moving from purely reactive, instruction-following GUI agents toward proactive task suggestion and personalized execution addresses critical limitations in existing mobile agent research.

Substantial and realistic longitudinal dataset: FingerTip 20K gathers 21,437 interaction episodes across 506 apps from 95 users over a full month of real-world device usage, providing rich contextual metadata (time, location scenario, historical intents, user profiles) that existing simulator-based or synthetic datasets lack.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The paper evaluates a broad spectrum of generalist vision-language models, GUI-specialized models (e.g., UI-TARS, CogAgent, Aguvis), and prompt-based agent frameworks, establishing realistic performance baselines and highlighting a substantial gap compared to human performance.

Extensive analysis and ablations: The appendix provides thoughtful supplementary investigations, including out-of-domain generalization across unseen users/apps/intents, modular vs. joint fine-tuning, context ablation (time, profile, scenario), and user studies validating the proposed personalization metric.
weaknesses: Limitations and brittleness of personalization evaluation metrics: The personalization metric Sim2 is defined as a ratio of string-level Levenshtein distances between linearized action sequences. Linear string representations can be sensitive to formatting, coordinates, and extraneous parameters rather than high-level semantic user habits.

Reproducibility and maintenance challenges on physical devices: The personalized execution evaluation was performed directly on physical Android devices connected via ADB across live third-party applications. Because commercial mobile apps constantly update UI elements, network responses, and authentication states, exactly reproducing these dynamic evaluation environments over time is difficult without a standardized sandboxed environment.

Geographic and demographic distribution: All 95 participants reside in mainland China and primarily interact with Chinese-language third-party applications. While the authors acknowledge this limitation, the narrow geographic and linguistic scope may limit immediate generalizability to global UI ecosystems.

Conflation of grounding failures with personalization in execution: Generalist models show near-zero execution success rates (SR2 1.0%–5.5%) primarily due to fine-grained coordinate grounding errors rather than a failure of intent understanding or personalization, making it hard to disentangle execution capability from personalization alignment.
